newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks tumble 2.01 pct in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks tumble 2.01 pct in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan stocks fell sharply in late trade on Monday as jitters over a deeply unsettled domestic political situation intensified selling, brokers said.
With 45 minutes to go, at 0315 GMT, the index had lost 166 points or 2.01 percent to 8,108.19 points. Turnover was T$105 billion.

Political uncertainties, including a cabinet reshuffle expected to be unveiled on Wednesday and opposition parties' demands that President Lee Teng-hui oust premier Lien Chan, have sapped investors' confidence, brokers said.
"It's a problem of lacking confidence," said Alex Yang, an analyst of National Securities.
Selling was across-the-board. Recent gainer United Micro lost T$1.5 or 2 percent to T$72.
Some brokers said government-related funds would intervene to support the market and stave off further falls.
